correctness.rationale: For all R>2, C_+≤R forces b≤R−1 and c(1+a)≤R−1. C_- strictly decreases in b,c for fixed other variables, so both saturate at any minimizer. With d=R−2>0, the remaining objective is [2(1+a)+max(2d+1,(1+a)/(a−1))]/d. The crossing a*=1+1/d and derivative 2−2/(a−1)^2 give unique optimum a=2 for d≤1 and a=a* for d≥1, yielding F(R)=9/d or 2+5/d+2/d². At d=1 both meet at a=2,b=2,c=2/3; F→2 as R→∞. Differentiating R F(R) gives d³−6d−4=(d+2)(d−1−sqrt(3))(d−1+sqrt(3)), with unique d≥1 minimum d=1+sqrt(3), product 9+6sqrt(3). Independently substituted six budgets in the original C± expressions. These are sharp bounds for this published proof, NOT sharp operator norms or universal isomorphism tradeoffs.
